You are a teaching assistant for a machine learning class. Write Python code that runs as is in Google Colab.

[Environment] Use only Colab's default libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn) and ucimlrepo. Print the scikit-learn version on the first line.
[Data] Load the concrete compressive strength data with 〔fetch_ucirepo(id=165) from ucimlrepo〕.
  - Features X: the 8 columns 〔cement, blast-furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, age〕 (name them in column order)
  - Target y: 〔compressive strength (MPa)〕 — it is a continuous number, so this is regression
[Rules]
  1) First split with train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=42), stratified by 3 grades that cut strength at 〔25, 45〕 MPa.
  2) Fit StandardScaler on the training data only; only transform the test data.
  3) Train with KNeighborsRegressor. Except for n_neighbors, pass arguments by name (weights="distance", etc.).
  4) Choose k by cross-validation inside the training data. Use the test data only once, for the final grading.
[Output] The chosen k, test R² and MAE, R² and MAE of a baseline that always answers the mean (DummyRegressor), and test R² without standardization.
[Forbidden] Do not train on the test data or choose k with it. Do not make up data.

bf6726ab403b.ko: KNN(k-최근접 이웃)은 새 배합이 오면 훈련 배합 전부와 거리를 재고, 가장 가까운 k개를 고른다. 그 이웃들의 강도를 평균 내면 회귀, "합격이 몇 표인가"로 다수결을 하면 분류다. 미리 배우는 것은 없다. 훈련 데이터를 통째로 외워 두었다가, 질문이 올 때마다 장부를 넘긴다.

bf6726ab403b.tr: When a new mix comes in, KNN (k-nearest neighbors) measures the distance to every training mix and picks the k nearest. Averaging those neighbors' strengths is regression; a majority vote on "how many votes for pass?" is classification. It learns nothing in advance. It memorizes the whole training set and flips through the ledger every time a question comes in.

7f6fd03d3099.ctx: ⟦5-4 로지스틱 회귀는 훈련 데이터로 가중치 9개를 고친 뒤 데이터를 버려도 됐다. KNN은 반대다. fit()이 하는 일은 훈련 데이터를 그대로 저장하는 것뿐이고, 모든 계산은 질문이 왔을 때 한다. 이런 방식을 게으른 학습(lazy learning) 또는 사례 기반 학습이라 부른다. 미리 식을 만들지 않으니 데이터 모양에 대한 가정도 거의 없다.⟧
7f6fd03d3099.tr: 5-4 logistic regression tuned 9 weights with the training data and could then throw the data away. KNN is the opposite. All fit() does is store the training data as is; every calculation happens when a question comes in. This is called lazy learning or instance-based learning. Since it builds no formula in advance, it makes almost no assumptions about the shape of the data.

d976f5055956.tr: Distance simply adds up the differences in each feature. A 20 kg difference in cement, a 20-day difference in age and a 20 kg difference in water are all "20." Yet 20 kg of water changes strength a lot, while 20 kg of coarse aggregate barely changes it. The last column of the table below is the average share each feature takes in the distance without standardization (its share of the variance). Water is only 1%, and superplasticizer only 0.1%. The features that matter most for strength are almost invisible in the distance. So we subtract each feature's mean and divide by its standard deviation. The mean and standard deviation come from the training data only.

1fe279fdab3d.ko: 지금의 scikit-learn(1.x)에서 KNeighborsRegressor와 KNeighborsClassifier는 첫 인자 n_neighbors만 이름 없이 넘길 수 있다. weights, metric 같은 나머지는 이름을 붙여야 하는 키워드 전용 인자다. KNeighborsRegressor(5, "distance")처럼 쓰면 TypeError가 난다. 위치로 넘기던 옛 코드를 보고 배운 AI가 자주 내는 실수다. 강도 같은 연속값을 분류기에 넣으면 ValueError: Unknown label type: continuous가 난다. 오류가 나는 실수는 차라리 친절하다. 시험지로 k를 고르는 실수는 오류 없이 점수만 부풀린다.

KNeighborsRegressor(5, "distance")처럼 쓰면 TypeError가 난다. 위치로 넘기던 옛 코드를 보고 배운 AI가 자주 내는 실수다. 강도 같은 연속값을 분류기에 넣으면 ValueError: Unknown label type: continuous가 난다. 오류가 나는 실수는 차라리 친절하다. 시험지로 k를 고르는 실수는 오류 없이 점수만 부풀린다.⟧
1fe279fdab3d.tr: In current scikit-learn (1.x), KNeighborsRegressor and KNeighborsClassifier let you pass only the first argument, n_neighbors, without a name. The rest, such as weights and metric, are keyword-only arguments that must be named. Writing KNeighborsRegressor(5, "distance") raises a TypeError. It is a common mistake by AI that learned from old code that passed them by position. Putting a continuous value such as strength into a classifier raises ValueError: Unknown label type: continuous. Mistakes that raise errors are actually kind. Choosing k with the exam paper raises no error and only inflates the score.

4cbabd3fd011.ko: 훈련 배합에게 "너와 가장 가까운 배합은?"이라고 물으면 자기 자신(거리 0)이 답한다. 그래서 k = 1의 훈련 점수는 외운 답을 읽는 것과 같다. 이 점수로 k를 고르면 늘 k = 1이 뽑힌다. 그래서 자기 자신을 빼고 맞히는 LOO(leave-one-out)로 잰다. KNN은 "하나 빼기"가 다시 학습할 필요 없이 거리표에서 한 줄을 지우면 끝나서, LOO가 특히 싸다.
4cbabd3fd011.ctx: ⟦훈련 배합에게 "너와 가장 가까운 배합은?"이라고 물으면 자기 자신(거리 0)이 답한다. 그래서 k = 1의 훈련 점수는 외운 답을 읽는 것과 같다. 이 점수로 k를 고르면 늘 k = 1이 뽑힌다. 그래서 자기 자신을 빼고 맞히는 LOO(leave-one-out)로 잰다. KNN은 "하나 빼기"가 다시 학습할 필요 없이 거리표에서 한 줄을 지우면 끝나서, LOO가 특히 싸다.⟧
4cbabd3fd011.tr: Ask a training mix "which mix is closest to you?" and it answers itself (distance 0). So the training score at k = 1 is like reading a memorized answer. If you choose k by this score, k = 1 always wins. That is why we measure with LOO (leave-one-out), which leaves the point itself out. For KNN, "leaving one out" needs no retraining; you just delete one line from the distance table, so LOO is especially cheap.

ce5582d109d5.tr: Data and calculations. The practical exam is the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength data, 1,030 mixes; the exam paper is the 258 mixes split with test_size=0.25, stratify=3 strength grades, random_state=42. The regression hiring bar is the R² that Mr. Manual's field formula (Abrams' law widened to the water–binder ratio and multiplied by the ACI 209R age correction, textbook constants as is, no learning) scored on the exam paper. The 35 MPa pass standard and the 25·45 MPa grade thresholds are values set for teaching. The numbers in Sections 01·02·04·05·06 and the interview result are calculated by this page, which measures distances directly in the browser (Euclidean distance; for equal distances, the mix with the smaller row number is picked first). Because some rows test the identical mix several times, when neighbors tie in distance at the k-th place, the chosen neighbors can differ from scikit-learn's, so results may differ slightly from Colab (Section A) in the third decimal place. The Section 06 curse-of-dimensionality chart uses uniformly distributed points generated with a fixed random seed. The 'AI-written code' in Section 03 is a deliberately constructed example collecting common mistakes, not an actual answer from any particular AI service.
